summary.rec_summary: 4 of 4 caches already supported on Redis OSS 7.x; Valkey 9 recommended as an optional cost-saving move for all 4

caches.name: aws_elasticache_replication_group.default

version_source.note: Module default var.engine_version = "7.1" (variables.tf:71), engine var.engine = "redis" (variables.tf:65), passed via local.engine_version (main.tf:10) to main.tf:185. Callers can override; null when global_replication_group_id is set.

caches.status_text: Supported. Optional: move to Valkey to cut cost.

risk_breakdown.signal: Single-node default with automatic failover off (cluster_size = 1, automatic_failover_enabled = false, multi_az_enabled = false)

caches.reason: Valkey is the AWS-recommended direction. The newest version gives the longest runway and your clients are compatible.

alternatives.tradeoff: Valkey 8.2 (confirm newest 8.x with DescribeCacheEngineVersions). About 20% lower node price than Redis OSS. One upgrade; rollback by snapshot restore only.
Keeps an in-place rollback to Redis OSS 7.1 while you validate. Costs a second change window later to reach Valkey 8/9.
Already on Redis OSS 7.1: stay as is. No Valkey discount and no newer engine features; end-of-support date for 7.x is not published yet.
Not recommended. A downgrade from 7.x is not possible in place, and Redis OSS 6 Extended Support charges start Feb 1, 2027.

cost_estimate.label: estimate
cost_estimate.basis: Redis OSS 7.x is in standard support; no Extended Support premium applies.

app_findings.signal: RBAC and TLS (AUTH token / in-transit encryption)
app_findings.impact: Low. Auth token and TLS carry over to Valkey; Valkey replication groups need in-transit encryption (module default is true, variables.tf:83).
app_findings.action: Confirm clients still authenticate and connect with TLS (rediss://) after the upgrade. Keep transit_encryption_enabled = true.

app_findings.action: Update dashboards, alarms or runbooks that reference the old parameter group name or engine 'redis'.

findings.title: All Redis OSS caches are already supported (Redis OSS 7.x)
findings.description: No Redis OSS 4, 5 or 6 caches were found. Every ElastiCache cache defined in this repository resolves to Redis OSS 7.0, 7.1 or Serverless major version 7, which are in standard support. No Extended Support exposure. Moving to Valkey is optional and reduces cost.

findings.title: Live data, AWS Health and Trusted Advisor not read (live_access=off)
findings.description: live_access=off was set, so no AWS API calls were made (no STS, ElastiCache, Health or Trusted Advisor). Versions and status come from the repository and AWS documentation. Drift was not checked. Rerun with live_access=auto and read-only credentials to confirm the running versions and detect drift.

findings.title: Custom parameter group on family redis7
findings.description: Created by default (create_parameter_group = true, variables.tf:261) with family var.family = "redis7" (variables.tf:50). Only caller-supplied parameters are set (default []); the complete example sets notify-keyspace-events = lK (examples/complete/main.tf:68), a dynamic parameter. A Valkey target needs family valkey9/valkey8/valkey7 with the same parameter values. Not set when global_replication_group_id is used (main.tf:8).

findings.title: AWS provider constraint >= 5.73.0 allows Valkey
findings.description: The root module requires hashicorp/aws >= 5.73.0, the release line that added engine = "valkey" for replication groups and Serverless caches. No provider major-version bump is needed (not a blocker). The examples declare looser constraints (>= 4.18, >= 5.32) but inherit the root constraint. Confirm Valkey 9 support in the provider version you pin.

findings.title: Global Datastore supported by input (not used by defaults)
findings.description: When a caller sets global_replication_group_id, engine, engine_version, parameter group and transit encryption are nulled (main.tf:8-15) and managed by the Global Datastore. Such a deployment would be a blocker for automatic remediation (secondary Regions upgrade first). Not used in this repository's examples.

findings.title: RBAC and TLS (AUTH token / in-transit encryption)
findings.description: Low. Auth token and TLS carry over to Valkey; Valkey replication groups need in-transit encryption (module default is true, variables.tf:83). Action: Confirm clients still authenticate and connect with TLS (rediss://) after the upgrade. Keep transit_encryption_enabled = true.

findings.title: RBAC user groups (user_group_ids / serverless_user_group_id)
findings.description: Low. Users and user groups passed in by the caller must use an engine compatible with the target. Action: If callers attach user groups, check their aws_elasticache_user / user_group engine values match the chosen target (redis or valkey). Serverless equivalent: user_group_id at main.tf:247.

findings.title: Monitoring / naming: parameter group name derived from family
findings.description: Low. The created parameter group name embeds the family (e.g. <id>-redis7), so it changes with the target family. Action: Update dashboards, alarms or runbooks that reference the old parameter group name or engine 'redis'.

findings.title: Pub/Sub keyspace notifications (notify-keyspace-events = lK)
findings.description: Low. Subscribers to keyspace events lose their connection during failover; delivery is at-most-once. Action: Resubscribe on reconnect. Confirm the parameter is carried into the new valkey parameter group.

warnings: Live data unavailable (live_access=off): running versions, drift, Health events and Trusted Advisor findings were not checked.
This is a reusable module; callers can override engine_version/family. Callers that pin Redis OSS 4, 5 or 6 are not visible here and must be analysed in their own repositories.
If a caller sets transit_encryption_enabled = false, a Valkey replication group target becomes a blocker (enable TLS with transit_encryption_mode = preferred first, or choose Redis OSS 7.1).
If a caller sets global_replication_group_id, the Global Datastore blocker applies.
Default and example caches are single-node with automatic failover off; the upgrade will cause a short outage rather than a failover.
Valkey 9.1 / Serverless major 9 availability in us-east-2 was not confirmed live; confirm with DescribeCacheEngineVersions before remediation.
next_step: No target has been applied. Create a remediation from these findings and choose a target. If you don't choose one, the recommended target is used.
